Voyager 1 · One light-day

Trajectory and distance: NASA/JPL Horizons. UTC dates and interpolated positions. The data begins about one hour after launch. The brief emergence from Earth is illustrative staging, not a reconstruction of the ascent.

The camera follows the actual trajectory. Body and spacecraft sizes are exaggerated for readability; lighting and sky orientation are illustrative. The endpoint is capped at the available data, with no extrapolation. Reference: NASA's one-light-day milestone. The final measurement connects the actual Earth and Voyager positions.

Spacecraft model: NASA/JPL-Caltech. Planet textures: Solar System Scope, CC BY 4.0, resized for the web.

Milky Way photograph: ESO/S. Brunier, CC BY 4.0. Original 6000 × 3000 panorama; mobile devices use up to 4096 × 2048. Background-only softening and highlight compression are applied at runtime. No AI-generated nebulae.

Voyager 1 archive: 22 photographs and mosaics from NASA/JPL and NASA/JPL-Caltech, covering Earth and Moon, the Jupiter and Saturn encounters, and the 1990 solar-system family portrait. Each gallery image includes its capture date, source and credit. Full provenance: image catalog. Dates are generally known to the day, not the exact exposure time; images from the same day have no claimed within-day order. Selected photographs appear briefly after their capture date during fast playback; all are available in the gallery. Mosaics and image-processing notes are identified in the viewer. Pale Blue Dot uses NASA's 2020 reprocessing of the 1990 exposures. Reuse follows the JPL image use policy.

Typography: Montserrat, The Montserrat Project Authors, SIL Open Font License 1.1. All runtime assets are bundled locally.
